ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (as amended by Ley 70 de 2019 and Executive Decree 489 of 2019) establishing the Panama AML/CFT legal framework; Decreto de Gabinete No. 128 de 2011 on the Panamanian Financial Action Task Force; Ley 129 de 17 de febrero de 2020 establishing the Beneficiarios Finales (UBO) Registry; Reglamento de la Ley 129 (Executive Decree No. 798 de 2020); Circulars of the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá and the Superintendencia de Sujetos No Financieros; plus AML/CFT rules applicable to Resident Agents under Resolution of the Superintendencia de Sujetos No Financieros.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, officers, authorized signatories, and beneficial owners against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HMT Sanctions List, and Panama's national Lista Oficial de Alertas issued by the Superintendencia de Sujetos No Financieros and the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF). Enhanced due diligence applies to all politically exposed persons (PEPs), foreign PEPs, family members, and close associates; negative media checks and source-of-funds verification are required. Resident agents must also file suspicious transaction reports (ROS) and maintain AML/CFT files for a minimum of five years after termination of the commercial relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá — Servicio en Línea (Sede Electrónica del Registro Público, accessible via https://www.registropublico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be written in alphabetic Latin characters and are accepted in Spanish or any modern language using the Latin alphabet; the official registered name in Panama is normally maintained in Spanish transliteration when any non-Latin script is used. The name must include a legal form denomitation such as 'Sociedad Anónima' or the abbreviation 'S.A.' and must not be misleading or identical or confusingly similar to an existing Panamanian trademark or registered company.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Uso de nombres de organismos oficiales nacionales o internacionales
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant or the licensed Panamanian attorney may file an administrative appeal (recurso de apelación) with the Dirección General del Registro Público de Panamá within five (5) business days of notification. The appeal must state the grounds of reconsideration, provide comparative justification against any cited conflicting registration, and may include amendments to the proposed name. If the appeal is denied, a new name reservation may be filed. A name reservation may be extended by requesting renewal before the expiration of the initial 30-day period and satisfying the corresponding renewal tariff, provided no competing application has been validated.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only where a licensed Panamanian resident agent maintains a physical office address in Panama and the corporate records and statutory registers are accessible at that address. A pure remote virtual office without a native resident agent is not acceptable. For a consumer Micro-SaaS entity engaged exclusively in online software subscription sales through payment aggregators, no physical local commercial premises are required; the registered office may be the resident agent's street address, provided all statutory registers are physically kept there and the UBO file is maintained.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low likelihood for a low-risk consumer Micro-SaaS issuer without local banking relationships: approximately 10% probability of a scheduled or unannounced on-site inspection by the Superintendencia de Sujetos No Financieros during the first operational year. Probability increases to approximately 25-35% if the entity later obtains a local Panama bank account, licenses payment services, or becomes a reporting financial institution. Resident agent inspection protocols require immediate production of corporate books, share ledger, UBO declarations, and accounting records.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 32 de 1927 (General Corporation Law of Panama), as amended, Arts. 1-72, including corporation formation, capital, registered office, resident agent, directors, and officers; supplemented by Law 23 of 2015 for beneficial-owner transparency requirements.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Personas Jurídicas (Public Registry of Panama, Legal Entities Section)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución (Public Incorporation Deed) with annexed Pacto Social y Estatutos
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. Authorized capital is commonly stated as US$10,000 divided into registered shares; no escrow, deposit, or immediate capitalization requirement is imposed by Panamanian law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the share subscriptions presented by the incorporator are ratified, and the subscribed shares are issued as fully paid or, if partially paid, as stated in the subscription list; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office located at [Address, Panama City] and the resident agent are adopted for statutory service; FURTHER RESOLVED, that [Name], [Name], and [Name] are appointed President, Secretary, and Treasurer, respectively; RESOLVED, that the President is authorized to execute all corporate, banking, tax, and regulatory documents and to indemnify agents as required to carry out the incorporation, registration, and licensing of the Corporation. These appointments shall take effect immediately and continue until successors are duly elected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Departamento de Personas Jurídicas / Online Registry Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a Panamanian corporate name request with two Spanish-language alternatives through the Public Registry’s online pre-inscription service or the Legal Entities counter. Pay the search fee and retain the issued certificate; the proposed name is reserved for a limited statutory period pending notarization and registration.
required_dossiers: Completed online name application form
Proposed corporate name and alternative in Spanish
Passport copy of incorporating shareholder or beneficial owner
Name search fee deposit receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to resemblance to an existing entity, select one of the cleared alternatives or file a consent/waiver from the existing company; the registry will issue a new clearance certificate without repeating substantive incorporation steps.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and notarization of the incorporation deed and registration before the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública of Panama and Registro Público de Panamá – Departamento de Personas Jurídicas
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Panamanian counsel drafts the Pacto Social and Estatutos; the incorporators execute the public deed before a licensed Panamanian notary. The notary forwards the protocolized copy to the Public Registry for inscription. The legal entity is formed upon issuance of the Registry folio certificate.
required_dossiers: Name availability certificate
Executed Escritura Pública with Pacto Social and Estatutos
Notarized corporate KYC of shareholders, directors, and officers
Statement of authorized capital and share classes
Payment receipt for Registry registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a defect notice, counsel files a written response curing the omission; for material amendments, the parties execute a clarifying public deed and the Registry re-runs the inscription without issuing a new legal-entity number.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First statutory board meeting and governance records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Office of the Corporation / Secretary / Resident Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first meeting of the board of directors at the registered office or remotely in accordance with the bylaws. Adopt the first board resolution ratifying share subscription, adopting the registered office and resident agent, appointing the President, Secretary and Treasurer, and authorizing banking and regulatory filings. Record minutes in the statutory minute book and issue stock certificates to shareholders.
required_dossiers: Notice of first board meeting or written consent form
Subscriber register and share subscription instrument
First board resolution text
Registered office resident-agent acceptance letter
Template share certificates and corporate seal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a quorum challenge or defective appointment is identified, convene an adjourned meeting or obtain unanimous written shareholder consent ratifying the officers; the corrected minutes are back-stamped and maintained in the corporate book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, municipal operating license, and physical environmental clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI – Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas); Municipio de Panamá; Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias; Ministerio de Ambiente; Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the RUC through the DGI online portal, then file the municipal Aviso de Operación with the local municipality and, for business activities, with MICI if required. For this office-based micro SaaS, no sectoral industrial license is required; verify lease zoning, submit fire-safety inspection, and file the Category I environmental registration with MiAMBIENTE where office equipment and e-waste handling apply.
required_dossiers: Registry certificate and certified copy of statutes
Copy of RUC form or DGI acknowledgment
Lease agreement for fiscal and registered address
Municipal Aviso de Operación application
Fire-safety inspection application and payment receipt
MiAMBIENTE Category I registration form where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a government authority queries the notice or inspection, submit missing zoning or fire documents within the cure period; any minor late-filing surcharge may be paid online. An unfavorable administrative resolution may be appealed to the competent superior administrative body.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) – Dirección General de Empresas, in coordination with the local Municipality for the Aviso de Operación
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación (Municipal Notice of Operation) and Municipal Commercial Operating License

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Verificación del Desempeño Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I (low impact) – environmental registration only; no full EIA report for office-based software operations without industrial facilities
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or industrial exhaust; office sewage connected to municipal sewer and subject to municipal discharge limits; no hazardous-waste generation; electronic waste handled by authorized recyclers; any emergency backup generator must comply with national fuel-storage safety and air-emission thresholds.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety inspection and certificate from the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá; structural and land-use compatibility confirmed by the municipal planning department for the leased office; occupational health and safety registration with MITRADEL if employees are engaged in Panama.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direccion General de Ingresos (DGI), subordinated to the Ministerio de Economia y Finanzas (MEF) of the Republic of Panama. The official digital platform for registration, filing, and fiscal interaction is the SIT (Sistema de Informacion Tributaria), accessible at https://sit.dgi.gob.pa.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Sociedad Anonima (S.A.) registration sequence: (1) execute the incorporation deed before a Panamanian notary through a licensed resident agent and record the company with the Registro Publico; (2) file the Aviso de Operacion with the relevant municipality if any physical or local business activity is conducted; (3) apply for the RUC (Registro Unico de Contribuyente) through the SIT portal, submitting the public deed, the appointment of the resident agent and legal representative, the Panamanian fiscal address, and the board resolution appointing the local compliance officer; (4) the RUC certificate will include the ITBMS taxpayer category and the applicable billing authorization; (5) for a micro-SaaS deriving revenue exclusively through foreign Merchant-of-Record platforms (Paddle, Lemon Squeezy), the S.A. should register with the DGI declaring the territorial source position (foreign-source software services) and, if projected Panamanian turnover does not exceed the statutory small-taxpayer threshold, consider electing the simplified small-taxpayer regime; (6) if the entity will issue invoices locally, request simultaneously the electronic invoicing (facturacion electronica) authorization from DGI, either through DGI-approved electronic billing software or an authorised fiscal printer.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not provide the United States style check-the-box election, nor does it maintain hybrid mismatch or CFC election mechanisms. The available statutory elections are: (i) the Regimen Simplificado de Pequenos Contribuyentes (unified annual quota of PAB 450) for taxpayers with gross annual income not exceeding PAB 36,000, excluding them from standard ITBMS remittance mechanics; (ii) the formal election to compute corporate income tax (ISR) on territorial-source income while attaching a detailed reconciliation of excluded foreign-source revenue; (iii) consolidated income tax filing for affiliated groups only where the statutory requirements of the Codigo Fiscal are satisfied; and (iv) advance rulings or advance pricing agreements requested from the DGI. As a territorial jurisdiction, Panama does not tax foreign-source income arising to the S.A., so no hybrid entity election is necessary or available under domestic law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto a las Transferencias de Bienes Muebles y Servicios), the Panamanian value-added tax governed by the Codigo Fiscal of the Republic of Panama.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Panama establishes no general ITBMS registration exemption threshold for corporations; all RUC holders that conduct taxable transfers of goods or services in Panama must charge, declare, and pay ITBMS. A special carve-out applies to small taxpayers under the Regimen Simplificado de Pequenos Contribuyentes: natural persons and small businesses whose gross annual revenue does not exceed PAB 36,000 (equivalent to USD 36,000 at the fixed PAB/USD peg) may elect a unified annual quota of PAB 450 and are released from the standard 7% ITBMS mechanics. Once annual revenue exceeds PAB 36,000, the taxpayer must withdraw from the simplified regime and comply fully with ITBMS registration, invoicing, and monthly declaration obligations. For the consumer micro-SaaS, if all end-consumer sales are invoiced by a foreign Merchant of Record (Paddle or Lemon Squeezy) that collects applicable destination taxes, the Panamanian S.A. has no Panamanian taxable turnover; nonetheless, the S.A. remains registered and may be subject only to the annual territorial ISR regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama operates a mandatory electronic invoicing (facturacion electronica) clearance model administered by the DGI. Issuers must be pre-authorised by the DGI and must use DGI-approved billing software or an authorised fiscal printer connected to the DGI environment. Each electronic invoice must be transmitted in near real time to the DGI platform through the web-service API of an accredited technology provider (Tercero Proveedor Autorizado, TPA) using the prescribed XML schema and the taxpayer's digital signature certificate; the DGI validates and returns a unique acceptance code that must appear on the invoice delivered to the customer. The system requires sequential numbering, tamper-evident digital stamping, and end-of-period reconciliation of voided and issued documents. For consumer micro-SaaS operations, where the payment platform acts as Merchant of Record, the foreign platform issues tax-compliant receipts to the final consumer in the relevant jurisdiction, while the Panamanian S.A. must issue valid electronic invoices only for its own service or licence fees charged to the MoR platform and for any Panamanian-sourced B2B supplies, which also remain subject to the e-invoicing mandate unless the taxpayer benefits from the small-taxpayer invoicing exception.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Panama's territorial ITBMS system, the export of services, including software subscription licences and digital cloud services, is eligible for a 0% ITBMS rate when the service is effectively used, consumed, or exploited outside Panama. The claimant must demonstrate: (i) the recipient is a foreign non-resident; (ii) the subscription, licence agreement, or service contract indicates offshore use; (iii) the payment is received from abroad, or from the foreign Merchant of Record settlement statement; and (iv) contemporaneous technical and accounting records show the foreign destination of the digital supply. Conversely, transactions with customers physically located in Panama remain subject to the standard 7% ITBMS; in the MoR flow, the payment platform is expected to collect and remit the applicable Panamanian tax on the B2C sale, with the S.A. retaining the export zero-rating only on its intercompany or intermediary fee.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration and removal permit (required only when software is shipped on physical media or cryptographic hardware; pure digital deliveries require no Panamanian customs declaration)
Bill of lading or airway bill (applicable to physical media shipments; for cloud deliveries, the cloud provisioning log and IP-address or geolocation evidence of foreign use)
Inward remittance certificate, SWIFT MT103 confirmation, or processor settlement statement from Paddle or Lemon Squeezy evidencing receipt of payment from abroad
Licence or subscription contract (EULA) with the foreign end customer, or the MoR consolidated subscriber report in machine-readable format identifying country of residence
Commercial invoice bearing a separate line item stating ITBMS 0% - Export of Services, together with the RUC and the DGI e-invoice acceptance code
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI routinely audits digital exporters claiming the 0% ITBMS rate, placing the burden of proof on the taxpayer to evidence foreign effective use of the service. Where the documentation is deficient or the service is recharacterised as a Panamanian taxable supply, the DGI will assess the unpaid 7% ITBMS, reverse any input tax credits, and apply statutory surcharges (recargos), monthly interest at the DGI quarterly rate, and the penalty provisions of the Codigo Fiscal, which may include fines calculated on the tax affected and, in cases of deliberate falsification, criminal sanctions under the Codigo Penal for tax fraud. Export refunds that have been obtained on the basis of simulated or supported invoices are subject to retrospective clawback with interest and penalties. Although Panama imposes no statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline because the balboa is pegged to the United States dollar, the 180-day convention is accepted for treasury substantiation and inward-remittance matching. The S.A. must therefore preserve the MoR settlement statements, DGI e-invoice logs, and bank credit records for the statutory limitation period, generally five years, to withstand DGI audit scrutiny.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: No traditional central bank exists in Panama. The Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) is the banking and foreign-currency regulatory authority; Banco Nacional de Panamá operates as a state-owned commercial bank, not a central bank. The US dollar is legal tender and provides the monetary anchor.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama operates under full dollarization and imposes no exchange-control restrictions on current or capital account transactions. Capital is freely convertible, inward investment is unrestricted, and profit remittance is not subject to central-bank approval. Practical remittance hurdles are limited to AML/KYC documentation obligations such as proof of source of funds, updated beneficial ownership records, and corporate good-standing certificates issued by the Registro Público.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement or mandatory conversion ratio in Panama. SaaS export receipts denominated in USD may be retained in Panamanian bank accounts or abroad. For regulatory clarity, banks require that export transactions be supported by commercial invoices, platform settlement reports, and, where relevant, the underlying service agreements to evidence the source of funds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (USD) and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account (USD) and Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium viability. Offshore digital EMI or fintech treasury providers such as Paddle, Lemon Squeezy, Wise, and Payoneer can be used as Merchant-of-Record or settlement rails for consumer SaaS subscriptions. They are not SBP-licensed banks and may not accept deposits or perform banking functions in Panama. Legal treasury design should maintain a primary Panamanian bank account for statutory capital, tax compliance, and local disbursements, while platform-based USD balances are used only as receivable clearing accounts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is generally feasible for low-risk corporate clients, subject to SBP-compliant e-KYC and video-identification procedures. In practice, SBP AML regulations require the effective identification of all beneficial owners and signatories; banks commonly require at least one director or the registered agent to complete an in-person or virtual meeting with the compliance officer before the signature card is activated. A foreign resident director may need to schedule a branch visit or a notarized and apostilled signature before a Panamanian consul if the bank does not accept remote identity verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Anonymous beneficial ownership or non-resident board with no Panamanian economic footprint
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide certified corporate extract, certificates of good standing from the Registro Público, full beneficial-ownership declaration form benefitting from the statutory exception to public disclosure, registered-agent certificate, certified passport copies, proof of residential address, and corporate org chart. Appoint the registered agent as co-signatory or authorize a power-of-attorney holder for bank communications.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds derived from high-volume global SaaS receipts through aggregators cannot be traced
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit Paddle/Lemon Squeezy settlement reports and transaction-level CSV exports, Merchant of Record contracts, recurring subscriber invoices, conversion/payment processor statements, Stripe/PayPal statements, tax return extracts showing the business activity, and a written flow-of-funds narrative covering the aggregation and net settlement process to the Panama treasury account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, or adverse media screening hit on a shareholder or director
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide certified explanations for any name matches, PEP declarations signed by directors, verdicts or official statements from sanctions authorities demonstrating no designation, comprehensive adverse media reports with dates and sources, passport biographical pages, professional reference letters, and certified background and bankruptcy checks from the jurisdiction of residence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained large one-time capital contribution or intercompany loan from foreign jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Evidence the lawful origin of funds through audited financial statements, shareholder net-worth certificate, bank reference letter from the remitting bank, executed loan or capital contribution agreement, certified board resolution approving the wiring, and a sworn statement of source of funds. The use of cash deposits must be fully avoided.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder capital injections must be routed by SWIFT MT103 from the overseas shareholder's bank to the Panama S.A. USD account. There is no Panamanian statutory purpose-code system, but the bank's swift text field 70 should state 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION TO PA_CORP, S.A. / EQUITY SUBSCRIPTION' and may include ISO purpose code 'COCP' or 'CRED' if the correspondent bank requires a codified classification. Verification includes a certified extract from the corporate share ledger, board resolution approving the share issuance, notarized placement certificate, and a sworn source-of-funds declaration. Given no minimum legal capital requirement, banks may still apply internal minimum operating deposits such as USD 1,000 to USD 10,000.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For SaaS operating expenses, the primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 for supplier and contractor payments, supported by physical or electronic commercial invoices and service agreements. For larger infrastructure or equipment purchases, a documentary commercial letter of credit governed by UCP600 is permissible. Panamanian domestic USD clearing is supported by the national Automated Clearing House and the camera de compensación; cross-border trade settlements flow through the international correspondent banking network. Each outbound payment must be accompanied by the underlying invoice, contract, or purchase order to satisfy SBP AML record-keeping duties.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright USD/EUR and USD/GBP forward contracts with SBP-licensed commercial banks or international counterparties; physical settlement in USD is the default given the Panamanian dollarized legal tender regime.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for minor or exotic currency exposures where physical delivery is not administratively practical; legally permissible under Panama's liberal foreign-exchange regime but generally redundant for a USD-functional-consumer-SaaS entity.

Cross-currency swaps for material multiyear commercial liabilities such as cloud infrastructure agreements, nearshore payroll obligations, or vendor leases; such swaps must be executed with institutionally approved counterparties and documented as treasury risk-management instruments rather than speculative positions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual legal entity tax - Impuesto Anual de Personería Jurídica (US$300 flat annual franchise tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) / Panama Treasury, paid through the resident agent or authorized banks
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 through January 15 of each calendar year for all existing Sociedades Anónimas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory late-payment surcharge plus interest calculated under the Código Fiscal; the company cannot obtain an official good-standing certificate (Personería Jurídica) while unpaid; continued non-payment over multiple years can lead to administrative strike-off by the Registro Público.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual income tax return - Formulario 105 (Declaración de Impuesto sobre la Renta); required only when the Panama S.A. derives Panama-source income. Dormant or offshore micro-SaaS companies without Panama-source income generally file no tax return but must maintain accounting records.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due no later than three months after fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year S.A., due by March 15 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fines, statutory interest, and penalties on assessed tax; tax clearance certificates are blocked and the DGI may prohibit transactions or withhold official certificates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO confirmation and beneficial-ownership update under Law 23 of 2015
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Resident agent as custodian; accessible to the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF), DGI, and other competent authorities upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least annually on the anniversary of incorporation and within 30 calendar days after any transfer of shares or change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines and supervisory sanctions for failing to maintain an accurate UBO register; the resident agent may refuse to execute instructions and may report non-compliance as a money-laundering red flag.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A micro-SaaS Panama S.A. is generally not subject to a mandatory independent audit. A certified audit by a Panamanian licensed CPA becomes compulsory when annual gross revenue exceeds approximately USD 1,000,000 or total assets exceed USD 2,000,000, or when the company operates in a regulated sector (banking, insurance, securities, or public-interest companies).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by IASB and adopted for Panamanian financial reporting; lower-risk micro entities may apply IFRS for SMEs or DGI-simplified local accounting standards while maintaining records sufficient to determine taxable income.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Law 23 of 2015 requires the Panamanian resident agent to maintain an updated register of ultimate beneficial owners. On each annual anniversary and after any share transfer, the company must deliver a certified UBO declaration identifying every natural person holding 10% or more or exercising control. The resident agent verifies the UBO schedule against the Register of Members and records the confirmation in the corporate file; share transfers must be reported to the agent promptly to allow the statutory register to be updated.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (share register and transfer endorsements)
Register of Directors and Officers (appointments, resignations, and committee designations)
Minute Book (shareholder and board resolution records)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - USD 6,000 when a Panamanian licensed CPA audit is triggered

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% flat rate on Panama-source taxable income of legal entities.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial taxation: only Panama-source income is subject to corporate income tax. Qualifying foreign-source subscription revenue of a consumer micro SaaS collected via Paddle or Lemon Squeezy can be entirely excluded, producing an effective 0% Panama tax on that revenue provided the company has no Panama fixed base, no Panamanian customer collection mechanics, and files the annual tax return showing foreign-source income. No general software tax holiday exists; a Panama-Pacifico special economic zone company may apply a 30% CIT reduction or an alternative low rate if physically licensed within the zone, but that is not assumed for this entity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 101 (Declaración Jurada Anual del Impuesto sobre la Renta) filed exclusively through the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) e-Tax portal (Sistema E-Tax / Sede Electrónica de la DGI).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For calendar-year taxpayers, the Form 101 is due on 31 March following the close of the fiscal year. For corporations using an off-calendar fiscal year, the due date is the last day of the third month following the fiscal year-end. Extension requests do not extend the statutory payment date; interest accrues from the original due date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) of the Panamanian S.A.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact RUC issued to the S.A. by the DGI. Non-resident shareholders must not enter their own foreign tax ID in this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year and closing date (Año Fiscal / Ejercicio Gravable).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the annual accounting period, e.g., 01/01/2024 to 31/12/2024. The period must match the audited financial statements if audited statements are required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross Panama-source receipts (Rentas brutas de fuente panameña).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all revenue from clients located in Panama, from services physically performed in Panama, and from contracts governed by Panamanian-source rules. If the micro SaaS has no Panamanian customers and no Panama delivery infrastructure, enter 0 and maintain source-location evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross foreign-source receipts (Rentas brutas de fuente extranjera).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter all subscription revenue earned from customers outside Panama through Paddle or Lemon Squeezy. Attach payout reports, merchant-of-record contracts, and customer country geolocation data to demonstrate non-Panama source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Costs and deductible expenses attributable to Panama-source income (Costos y gastos deducibles).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only costs and expenses directly linked to the production of Panama-source income are deductible in the Caribbean/Panama territorial allocation. Foreign-source costs such as foreign servers, foreign support contractors, and overseas marketing paid by the S.A. are not deductible against foreign-source receipts.

Computed as Line 101-01 minus Line 101-03, plus required add-backs. In a pure foreign-source micro SaaS, net taxable income should be 0 unless the DGI recharacterizes revenue as Panama-source under substance-over-form rules.
Enter 0 if Line 101-04 is 0. If the DGI reclassifies any revenue as Panama-source, tax is payable at 25% plus the applicable surcharge.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prepayments, withholdings, and tax credits (Pagos acreditados).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim credits for Panama-source withholding taxes suffered on revenue, and any quarterly advance payments made during the year. Foreign income taxes are not creditable because of Panama's territorial system.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable or refund (Resultado a pagar o saldo a favor).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay balances into Banco Nacional de Panamá using the DGI payment voucher. Refunds are subject to DGI audit; non-resident owned S.A.s should verify beneficial owner identity before claiming refunds.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file Form 101 on time triggers a minimum penalty of USD 50 or 10% of the annual tax due, whichever is greater. Late payment attracts a 1% monthly surcharge up to a maximum of 25%, plus interest at the DGI's statutory rate of 10% per annum. False filing with intent to evade tax adds a 100% surcharge and criminal liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 102 (Declaración Temporal / Anticipo de Impuesto sobre la Renta) filed through DGI e-Tax.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly advance payment declarations are due within the first 30 days after the end of each quarter for corporations with prior-year taxable income exceeding a de minimis threshold. Micro SaaS entities with nil Panama-source taxable income are generally still expected to submit a zero Form 102 if the DGI has issued a payment code.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly taxable base estimate (Base imponible estimada del trimestre).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident controlled S.A.s should report zero if all revenue is foreign-source and no Panama-source operations exist.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance tax rate and amount payable (Tasa del anticipo y monto a pagar).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The standard rate is 25% of estimated Panama-source taxable income for the quarter. Foreign-source income is not included.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior quarterly prepayments and credits (Anticipos anteriores y créditos).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Panama tax prepayments are creditable. Do not attach foreign taxes paid on foreign-source SaaS revenue.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Under Panama Tax Code article 114 and related regulations, failure to file or underpayment of quarterly prepayments is penalized with 10% of the omitted amount, plus monthly interest of 1% and indexation in aggravated cases. Repeated omissions before 31 March can trigger immediate DGI collection proceedings.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on declared dividends paid out of Panama-source taxable profits. Dividends paid out of foreign-source profits that were never subject to Panamanian corporate income tax may be subject to the same 10% dividend withholding if the DGI considers the distribution to be a taxable dividend from a Panamanian legal entity. For this reason, the prudent default position for a Panama S.A. is that all dividend distributions to shareholders, irrespective of the underlying source of profit, carry a 10% withholding tax unless the company obtains a specific DGI source ruling or applicable treaty reduction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Where a double taxation agreement (DTA) is in force between Panama and the shareholder's country of residence, treaty relief is not automatic. The non-resident shareholder must deliver to the paying S.A.: (1) a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the shareholder's competent tax authority; (2) a declaration of beneficial ownership and absence of a Panama permanent establishment; and (3) an indemnity that the shareholder will notify any material change. The S.A. must submit the TRC and supporting forms through the DGI e-Tax system and obtain a concession/resolution recognizing the reduced rate before applying it. In practice, the DGI requires the withholding agent to maintain the underlying documents for six years and to apply the statutory 10% rate until the relief has been granted.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on cross-border royalties for the use of IP and on debt interest paid to non-residents generally stands at 12.5% under Panama's non-resident income-tax rules. Treaty rates may reduce the royalty rate to 0% or 5%, and interest to 0%, 5% or 10%, depending on the specific DTA and the application of limitation-on-benefits clauses. If the non-resident lender has no Panama permanent establishment and the loan is booked and serviced abroad, the interest can qualify for exemption under Panamanian source rules only if the DGI accepts the foreign-source character; otherwise withholding applies.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD 5,000,000 of annual gross income is the mandatory threshold for a Panamanian taxpayer to prepare and submit transfer pricing documentation (Local File) for related-party transactions. Master File documentation is required once the multinational group's consolidated revenues exceed USD 50,000,000, and Country-by-Country Reporting applies at the USD 750,000,000 group revenue threshold. The target consumer micro SaaS, assuming far lower revenue, falls below the mandatory Local File threshold but must still be able to demonstrate arm's length pricing if challenged by the DGI.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Requirements (ESR), introduced by Law 254 of 2020 and regulated by Executive Decree 743 of 2021, apply to Panamanian tax-resident legal entities and private interest foundations performing relevant activities. For a micro SaaS company, the relevant activity classification may be 'holding company' or 'provision of digital services', depending on actual functions. To maintain the 0% effective tax rate on foreign-source income and to avoid reclassification as a shell, the S.A. must demonstrate local substance: physical office or leased space in Panama, at least one employee or independent contractor with management authority, participation in strategic decisions in Panama, and maintenance of full corporate accounting records in Panama. An annual ESR declaration must be filed with the DGI. Failure to file or satisfy substance requirements voids the territorial-source exclusion and may trigger deemed Panama-source income determination.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The S.A. reports all SaaS subscription revenue as foreign-source while local operations in Panama actually generate or monetise the software, or the entity uses Paddle/Lemon Squeezy as a mere collection conduit to conceal Panamanian taxable income from Panamanian customers. Also includes the deliberate omission of intra-group payments for software code, trademarks, or data assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of the evaded tax, a surcharge of 50% to 100% for fraudulent misrepresentation, annual interest of 10%, and administrative fines under Panama's Tax Code articles 158-171. Criminal tax evasion is punishable by imprisonment for two to five years under Law 38 of 2001.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns or direct the mischaracterisation of source are jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax debt. Panama courts may pierce the corporate veil, order civil restitution, seize personal assets, prohibit travel (travel ban / impedimento de salida) and impose imprisonment on the responsible directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The S.A. operates as a letterbox entity with only a registered agent address, no payroll, no physical office, no local board meetings, and no local accounting records; it claims foreign-source exemption on high subscription revenue while all functions are performed by a foreign parent or a third-party service provider outside Panama.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 254 of 2020, ESR non-compliance attracts administrative penalties ranging from USD 50,000 to USD 200,000, with potential strike-off or dissolution of the S.A. The DGI may reject the foreign-source exclusion and impose 25% CIT on a deemed profit of at least 20% of gross revenue, plus 10% dividend withholding and TP adjustments with a 50% penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The statutory director, resident agent, and beneficial owner may be jointly liable for ESR penalties and tax deficiencies. Panama has increasingly issued foreign travel bans and asset freezes against directors of non-compliant shell companies; the resident agent's license can be suspended for repeated violations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering / Beneficial Ownership Filing Offence
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file or update the mandatory Panamanian beneficial owner registry (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales) for the S.A.; accepting anonymous subscription payments without customer due diligence; transferring profits to unknown nominees; or using Paddle/Lemon Squeezy payouts as a layer for undisclosed third-party funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 23 of 2015 and Law 129 of 2020, administrative fines for AML breaches can reach USD 1,000,000 for legal entities. Criminal money laundering carries imprisonment from five to twelve years, based on the aggregate funds involved. The Financial Analysis Unit (UAF) may order a freeze of the S.A.'s bank accounts and revocation of the registered agent mandate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and resident agents are criminally liable if they knowingly allow the S.A. to be used as a laundering vehicle. Personal liability includes imprisonment, extradition on international warrants, confiscation of personal property, and permanent prohibition from serving as directors in Panama. Travel bans are routinely applied to the individuals controlling the shell.
